findings.Q002: Actual MereSessions/GraphSession consumer: a correct checkpoint opens as a control; replacing graph.json and facets.json while retaining its in-range cursor makes open report the original session/journal but return a foreign graph. graph_at at the same cursor reconstructs the real baseline+journal. Ahead checkpoint falls back to real replay.
findings.Q032: Actual stored legacy session via MemoryBackend: applied initial and changed method/evidence on the same handle, loaded a new session instance, successfully qualify_legacy, and opened again. Changed reason survives stored translation. Checked exact-ID writer refuses each changed reason as a control.

limits: The checkpoint test substitutes valid stored checkpoint documents; it does not demonstrate spontaneous corruption or bypass of operating-system permissions.
Translated legacy checkpoints have a replay comparison; the substituted-checkpoint diagnostic targets ordinary recorded sessions.
No product UI or external receiving host acceptance claim.
The first attempt failed to compile because Seq was imported from Pandect instead of Muniment; initial source/output are retained.
Both diagnostics use MemoryBackend and in-process new session instances. These prove public session/store admission behavior, not disk durability or a fresh-process recovery gate.
